analysis: The only change in scripts/test-install-atomic.sh is a new regression test at head lines 474-481. It runs the installer under `umask 077` and asserts that the installed fan helper is mode 755 and pagedattention.metal is mode 644. The stated intent is that the installer extracts the bundle under umask 022, so a restrictive caller umask cannot leave release files owner-only. This is test-only code. It adds no runtime attack surface, does not touch production trust paths, and weakens no existing assertions. The surrounding checks stay in place: no CLT tools referenced, no privileged install in install.sh, fan-helper variant rejection, payload hash checks, designated-requirement verification, and the App Attest smoke marker check. The new test strengthens the permission invariant on the root-adjacent fan helper (TB-010, T-045). It requires the helper to be 0755 rather than group- or world-writable, and its ownership stays with the installing user, not root. The change does not alter TB-011 or TB-003 assumptions. install.sh is not in the supplied evidence, so I could not confirm that the installer actually sets umask 022. That is a test-coverage question, not a regression, and I raise no finding on it. One caveat: the test lives in a script that runs a pre-existing and unchanged umask path, and the new test would simply fail if the installer did not implement it.
